blindSummary: Regional record: a highly visible LGBT urban scene, total anonymity in daily life, a very large annual Pride event. This state/province is the one unit that has used its own legislative power to narrow trans law - two laws (both 27 December 2023) amended its own 2016 gender-identity law and its anti-LGBTBI law on the stated ground of protecting freedom of expression and academic freedom, stripping the provisions that obliged educational institutions; a 2022 education law centres parents as primary responsible parties and structures school opt-outs (an opt-out mechanism in this state/province's schools). Evidentiary caveat: citizens of this state/province report LGTBI hate-crime offences to reporting services more than those of any other state/province, so the low recorded hostility here must not be read as low incidence - the divergence is in recording rules, not in reality.
blindSourceSummaries: Official state-gazette text of a 2023 trans-equality law (28 February 2023) establishing self-ID legal gender recognition (16+, no diagnosis), broad anti-discrimination guarantees, employment and health measures, and an LGBTI equality strategy. National framework that this state/province's 2023 amendments sit beside.
An international human-rights organisation (Feb 2023) hails this country's self-ID gender-recognition law as a hard-won victory after years of activism. National framework context.

A criminal-law firm analysis in this country (June 2026): disentangles three statutes - what the 2023 equality law does and does not do; the discrimination aggravating factor of a penal-code provision (gender identity/expression motives); and a hate-offences provision extended to trans/LGBTI people. National framework context.
blindLocalsOnly: Resident-facing: the 2023 state/province-level amendments that removed the 2016 trans-law obligations on educational institutions, and the 2022 education law's parental-primary-responsibility and school opt-out mechanism, shape school environments for local families.
